finding.claim: Blind SSRF: the iconUrl value from PUT /profile is stored with no validation and later fetched server-side by the nightly sync job. Any authenticated user who can update their profile can make the server issue GET requests to arbitrary URLs, including internal hosts, loopback and cloud metadata endpoints such as http://169.254.169.254/. The response body is read into a byte array and not returned in this file, so impact is mainly blind internal requests and port or host probing. It could escalate if the bytes are later stored or served as the icon.

trace.note: update(webhook, icon) receives the request values
this.iconUrl = icon stored with no scheme, host or IP validation
sync() calls URI.create(iconUrl) and sends a GET from the server in the nightly job

finding.guards_checked: No validation is applied to iconUrl. The regex on line 12 covers only webhook. There is no scheme allowlist, no host allowlist, no private, loopback or link-local IP blocking, and no DNS pinning. The HttpClient is passed in and its configuration is not visible; the Java default does not follow redirects, which does not help here because the initial URL is already attacker-chosen.

verdict.reason: src/Profile.java:16 stores the request-supplied icon unvalidated (the regex at line 12 covers only webhook), and src/Profile.java:23 fetches it server-side via URI.create(iconUrl) with no scheme or host guard. The "PUT /profile" route is only a comment at line 10, and the file contains no authentication check, so the "authenticated user" part of the source is unconfirmed, but the value is request-controlled.
